workingTitle: The Loan Cap Most Investors Hit at Exactly 10 Properties

beats.line: Most investors hit a wall at exactly 10 properties — and most don't know why until they're there.
It's not the market. It's not your credit. It's a hard rule most banks never explain up front.
Fannie Mae caps conventional mortgages at 10 total financed properties per borrower — including the home you live in.
Hit that number, and your bank can't write you an eleventh conventional loan. Not won't — legally can't.
This is why serious investors move to DSCR loans once they scale past a handful of properties.
A DSCR loan doesn't look at your personal income or your tax returns. It asks one question: does the property's rent cover its own mortgage payment?
Most DSCR lenders want that ratio around 1.0 to 1.25 — the rent covering 100% to 125% of the payment.
Because each property is judged on its own, there's no 10-property ceiling. The eleventh loan doesn't carry the weight of the first ten.
It also means self-employed investors who write off income on paper — the same write-offs that help at tax time — don't get penalized when qualifying for the loan.
DSCR loans usually cost more than a conventional mortgage in rate and down payment — the tradeoff for skipping the personal-income underwriting.
10 properties is where conventional financing legally stops. DSCR is how investors keep scaling past it.
If you're getting close to that number — or already past it — this is the financing conversation to have before your next deal, not after your tenth loan gets denied.
